title: The Quiet Correlation
thesis: A shipping-lane diversion and a grocery bill moved together this spring, a mechanical correlation hidden only by the lag and by the fact that each story was filed to a different desk.
body:
No one announced a connection between a shipping lane and a grocery bill, but the two moved together this spring. As carriers diverted around the Red Sea, container rates climbed — and a month later the goods half of the inflation print followed them up [sy_9caae79effac, sy_466f4024101b].

The thread is unglamorous and entirely mechanical: a longer route is a higher cost, and a higher cost arrives, eventually, at the till. The lag is the only thing that hides it [sy_9caae79effac, sy_466f4024101b].

What makes the correlation quiet is that each story was filed to a different desk. Logistics reported the diversions; the macro desk reported the print; almost no one drew the line between them [sy_466f4024101b].
